drafter.private_reasoning: The draft leaves material commercial terms undefined. Prioritize a workable agreement and client protection rather than speed or referral interests. Do not disclose confidential client information or make unsupported assurances about liabilities. Obtain client instructions on representations, disclosure obligations, and indemnity limits before execution.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our initial revisions clarifying payment, closing mechanics, the financial-statement representation, and indemnity procedure. The purchase price, relevant schedules, closing conditions, and indemnity limitations remain subject to agreement. This draft remains subject to client review and approval and is not ready for execution.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller the purchase price for the Shares by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller in writing. The purchase price, any adjustment mechanism, and any escrow or holdback shall be expressly agreed in writing and incorporated into this Agreement before execution.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable closing conditions. The parties shall agree the closing conditions, required approvals, deliverables, and consequences of a failure to close before execution.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Subject to the disclosure schedules delivered and agreed in connection with execution of this Agreement, the Seller represents that the financial statements identified in an agreed schedule fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the relevant business for the periods stated, in accordance with the accounting principles specified in that schedule, consistently applied, subject to any exceptions expressly identified in that schedule.

4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the scope, exclusions, survival periods, thresholds, caps, and claim procedures to be expressly agreed before execution, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual losses arising from liabilities attributable to periods before Closing that were not disclosed in this Agreement or the agreed disclosure schedules. The Buyer shall provide reasonably prompt written notice describing each claim and its basis, take reasonable steps to mitigate recoverable losses, and shall not recover more than once for the same loss. The parties shall agree procedures for the defense and settlement of third-party claims before execution.

Offer concrete proposed mechanics and protections, expressly subject to client approval, while identifying the missing price and schedules as execution blockers. Use visible drafting only; do not imply that diligence is complete or that undisclosed liabilities do not exist.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We propose the attached revisions for discussion, subject to client approval and without deemed acceptance. They provide a firm 60-day closing long-stop, express termination remedies, a financial-statement representation without a blanket disclosure qualifier, and indemnity coverage for pre-Closing liabilities whether disclosed or not, subject to the stated proposed limitations. We propose a cash-free, debt-free price adjustment mechanism and a 10% indemnity escrow. The base purchase price, working-capital target, financial-statement schedule, and supporting schedules remain outstanding; we cannot responsibly supply figures or schedules that have not been verified and authorized. The agreement is not execution-ready, and neither silence nor circulation constitutes acceptance. Please provide your proposed base price and working-capital target and identify any requested changes to the proposed limitations so that we can seek instructions on a consolidated package.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The base purchase price for the Shares shall be [amount and currency to be expressly agreed before execution]. The transaction shall be on a cash-free, debt-free basis, with the base purchase price increased by Closing cash, decreased by Closing indebtedness and unpaid Seller transaction expenses, and increased or decreased by the amount by which Closing working capital exceeds or falls below the agreed target. Definitions, the target, accounting policies, and an illustrative calculation shall be included in an agreed purchase-price schedule before execution; no item shall be counted more than once. Seller shall deliver a good-faith estimated Closing statement at least five business days before Closing. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the estimated adjusted price, less an escrow equal to 10% of the base purchase price, by wire transfer to Seller's designated account, and deposit the escrow with an independent escrow agent under an agreed escrow agreement. Buyer shall deliver a final Closing statement within 60 days after Closing. Seller shall have 30 days to object with reasonable particulars; undisputed items shall become final. Disputed items remaining after 20 days of good-faith negotiations shall be referred to an independent accountant jointly appointed by the parties, acting as an expert and deciding only disputed items within the parties' submitted ranges. The accountant's determination shall be final absent manifest error, with fees allocated in proportion to each party's unsuccessful disputed amounts. Any resulting payment shall be made within five business days after final determination. The indemnity escrow shall be released 18 months after Closing, less amounts reasonably reserved for timely notified unresolved claims; amounts reserved shall be released promptly upon resolution.
edits.name: Proposed economics and adjustment mechanics

edits.text: 2. CLOSING; TERMINATION. Closing shall occur on the fifth business day after satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable closing conditions, and in any event no later than 60 calendar days after signing (the Long-Stop Date). Conditions shall include receipt of all legally required transaction approvals and absence of any law or order prohibiting Closing; Buyer's conditions shall also include Seller's delivery of duly executed share-transfer instruments, evidence of title and release of liens on the Shares, and a certificate confirming that Seller's representations are accurate at Closing in all material respects and its pre-Closing covenants have been performed in all material respects. Seller's conditions shall include Buyer's delivery of the Closing funds and a corresponding certificate concerning Buyer's representations and covenants. Each party shall use reasonable efforts to satisfy the conditions applicable to it. Either party may terminate by written notice if Closing has not occurred by the Long-Stop Date, unless that party's material breach principally caused the failure to close. A nonbreaching party may also terminate for the other party's material breach that prevents satisfaction of a closing condition and remains uncured ten business days after written notice, or is incapable of cure before the Long-Stop Date. Termination ends future performance obligations but does not affect accrued rights, liability for prior breach, confidentiality obligations, or available damages and equitable remedies, without duplicate recovery. Any additional conditions, approvals, or deliverables must be expressly agreed and listed before execution.
edits.name: Firm long-stop and termination remedies

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents that the financial statements identified in the financial-statement schedule fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the relevant business for the periods stated, in accordance with the accounting principles specified in that schedule, consistently applied. This representation is not qualified by general disclosures, any data-room material, or blanket incorporation of disclosure schedules. Any exception must be specifically described in the financial-statement schedule, expressly identify this representation, and be expressly accepted in writing by Buyer before execution. The schedule shall identify the statements, periods, applicable accounting principles, and any specifically negotiated qualifications for unaudited statements. Seller shall deliver the identified statements and supporting schedules for review before execution; their delivery alone does not constitute Buyer's acceptance of any exception.
edits.name: Specific financial-statement representation

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual losses arising from liabilities attributable to periods before Closing, whether or not disclosed, and from breaches of Seller's representations or covenants. Disclosure alone shall not exclude a liability from this indemnity. An exclusion requires a specific written exception expressly accepted by Buyer and incorporated into this Agreement before execution. Claims for breaches of representations other than title to the Shares, capacity, and authority must be notified within 18 months after Closing; claims under the separate pre-Closing liability indemnity must be notified within 36 months after Closing. Claims concerning title, capacity, authority, taxes, and covenants survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statutory limitation period. Timely notified claims survive until resolved. A deductible equal to 0.5% of the base purchase price and an aggregate cap equal to 20% of the base purchase price apply collectively to ordinary representation claims and the separate pre-Closing liability indemnity. Claims concerning title, capacity, authority, taxes, and covenants are excluded from that deductible and cap but are subject to an aggregate liability ceiling equal to the base purchase price. These limitations do not limit liability for Seller's fraud or any liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Escrow is security and not Buyer's exclusive recourse. Buyer shall provide reasonably prompt written notice describing each claim and its basis and, to the extent reasonably ascertainable, its amount; delay bars recovery only to the extent Seller is materially prejudiced. Buyer shall take reasonable steps to mitigate losses and shall not recover twice for the same loss, including amounts already reflected in the final purchase-price adjustment. Seller may assume the defense of a third-party claim with reasonably acceptable counsel only if it acknowledges its indemnity obligation and the claim seeks solely monetary relief without a material conflict of interest. Buyer may participate at its own expense, except that Seller shall bear reasonable separate-counsel costs where a material conflict exists. No settlement may impose an admission, nonmonetary obligation, or unreleased liability on Buyer without Buyer's written consent. If Seller does not timely assume a permitted defense, Buyer may defend and reasonably settle the claim after consultation with Seller. All proposed percentages, periods, exceptions, and limitations remain subject to express agreement before execution.
edits.name: Disclosed and undisclosed pre-Closing liability protection

receiver.message_back: Subject to client approval and agreement of the complete execution documents, Buyer proposes a 15% escrow held for 36 months, a 0.5% tipping basket and 30% cap for ordinary representation claims, and no basket with a purchase-price cap for the separate pre-Closing liability indemnity; the existing carve-outs and nonexclusive escrow recourse should remain. We will provide an authorized base-price proposal and a working-capital target following review of verified financial statements and supporting schedules; meanwhile, the 60-day long-stop and express termination remedies are acceptable in principle only, without acceptance of the package or outstanding limitations.
